subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If x + iy = 1/(1 + cos θ + i sin θ), then show that 4x² − 1 = 0.

mark_split.label: Rewrite the denominator with half angles
Multiply by the conjugate and simplify

recall_prompt: Say how you would show 4x² − 1 = 0 — what identities you use on the denominator, what you multiply by, and which part you read off at the end.
insider_note: Everything after depends on the first line: 1 + cos θ = 2cos²(θ/2) and sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2)·cos(θ/2) share the factor 2cos(θ/2), and taking it out of the whole denominator is the step the other three marks depend on. Only the real part x is used at the end — time spent simplifying y brings no mark.

steps.label: Use half angles
steps.margin_note: First mark. The two identities 1 + cos θ = 2cos²(θ/2) and sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2) share the factor 2cos(θ/2). Taking it out is the key step of the question.
steps.memory_tip: 1 + cos θ = 2cos²(θ/2) and sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2) share the factor 2cos(θ/2). Take it out of both.

recall.must_convey: That 1 + cos θ and sin θ are written with half angles so the denominator becomes 2cos(θ/2) times [cos(θ/2) + i sin(θ/2)].
accept: write one plus cos theta as two cos squared theta by two and sin theta as two sin theta by two cos theta by two
use half angle identities and take two cos theta by two common from the denominator
the denominator becomes two cos theta by two times cos theta by two plus i sin theta by two
half angle formulas use chesi two cos theta by two common teeyali
factor two cos of half theta out of the denominator

steps.why: In the form 2cos(θ/2)·cis(θ/2) the denominator is a real number times a unit complex number, and the unit complex number has an easy conjugate. Without the half angles the division is much longer.
common_mistakes: Using 1 + cos θ = 2sin²(θ/2) — that is 1 − cos θ.
Writing sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2) and forgetting the cos(θ/2).
Taking 2cos(θ/2) out of the first term only.

steps.label: Divide by the conjugate
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Multiply above and below by cos(θ/2) − i sin(θ/2). The bracket product is cos² + sin² = 1, so only 2cos(θ/2) is left underneath, and it cancels the cos(θ/2) on top of the real part.
steps.memory_tip: (cos A + i sin A)(cos A − i sin A) = 1, so only 2cos(θ/2) is left underneath.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying by the conjugate cos(θ/2) − i sin(θ/2) leaves x + iy = 1/2 − (i/2) tan(θ/2), because cos² + sin² = 1.
accept: multiply by cos theta by two minus i sin theta by two, the bracket product is one, and x plus i y becomes half minus i by two tan theta by two
rationalise with the conjugate, cos squared plus sin squared is one, so it is half minus i half tan of theta by two
after dividing by the conjugate the real part is half and the imaginary part is minus half tan theta by two
conjugate tho multiply cheste half minus i by two tan theta by two vasthundi
the result is one by two minus i tan theta by two over two

steps.why: The point of the conjugate is that (cos A + i sin A)(cos A − i sin A) = cos²A + sin²A = 1 — the i is removed from the denominator with no extra work. Then cos(θ/2)/(2cos(θ/2)) = 1/2 is the real part, and it does not depend on θ at all.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by cos(θ/2) + i sin(θ/2) again instead of the conjugate.
Forgetting the 2cos(θ/2) that stays in the denominator.
Writing the imaginary part as −(1/2) sin(θ/2) instead of −(1/2) tan(θ/2).

steps.label: Compare real parts
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Only x is needed. Read it off, square, and rearrange into the form asked.
steps.memory_tip: x = 1/2 for every θ. Only x is needed — square it and rearrange, and leave y alone.

recall.must_convey: That comparing real parts gives x = 1/2, so 2x = 1 and squaring gives 4x² − 1 = 0.
accept: the real part is half so two x is one and squaring gives four x squared minus one equals zero
x equals half, so four x squared equals one
compare real parts, x is one by two, square two x equals one
real part half kabatti two x equals one, square cheste four x square minus one zero
x is a half and that gives four x squared minus one is zero

steps.why: The question asks about x only, so the imaginary part is not needed once the division is done. x = 1/2 for every θ is the fact; 4x² − 1 = 0 is just that fact written in the form the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Also equating imaginary parts and trying to use y — not needed here.
Writing x = 1/2 and stopping without reaching 4x² − 1 = 0.
